subject: biology
title: Krebs Cycle & Oxidative Phosphorylation Adventure
welcome_lead: Today you'll cycle through Krebs and ride the electron transport chain to make ATP via chemiosmosis.
meta_desc: A-Level Biology Respiration — Krebs cycle in the matrix, electron transport chain on the inner membrane, chemiosmosis and ATP synthase.
final_note: You learned that the Krebs cycle produces 3 NADH, 1 FADH2, 1 ATP and 2 CO2 per acetyl CoA, and oxidative phosphorylation uses these reduced coenzymes to make ~34 ATP via chemiosmosis.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Each turn starts with acetyl CoA joining oxaloacetate (4C) → citrate (6C).

Per turn (per acetyl CoA), the cycle produces:
- 3 NADH
- 1 FADH₂
- 1 ATP (substrate-level)
- 2 CO₂

It runs twice per glucose. Total so far: 4 ATP + 10 NADH + 2 FADH₂.

The ETC sits on the inner mitochondrial membrane (lots of cristae = huge surface area).

NADH and FADH₂ donate electrons → pass down protein carriers, releasing energy.

That energy pumps H+ from matrix → intermembrane space, building a proton gradient.

At the end, O₂ accepts electrons + H+ → H₂O (final electron acceptor).

H+ ions can only return through one channel: ATP synthase.

As they flow down their gradient, the enzyme rotates and joins ADP + Pi → ATP.

Yield rule of thumb:
- 1 NADH → ~2.5 ATP
- 1 FADH₂ → ~1.5 ATP

Total: about 30–32 ATP per glucose (older textbooks quote up to 38).
